{{Short description|Norwegian chemist and metallurgist}}
'''Terkel Nissen Rosenqvist''' (2 October 1921 – 1 April 2011) was a [[Norway|Norwegian]] [[chemist]] and [[metallurgy|metallurgist]].

== Biography ==
He was born in [[Aker, Norway|Aker]]. His parents were businessman Einar Rosenqvist (1892–1962) and Julia (Mulka) Marija Kos (1893–1939). His brother was [[Ivan Th. Rosenqvist]]. From 1945 to 1963 he was married to Tone Barth (January 25, 1924 – October 10, 1980), the sister of Professor of Social Anthropology [[Fredrik Barth]] (born 1928).<ref name=hvem>{{cite encyclopedia| year=1973| title=Rosenqvist, Terkel| encyclopedia=[[Hvem er hvem?]]| editor=Steenstrup, Bjørn| publisher=Aschehoug| location=Oslo| url=https://runeberg.org/hvemerhvem/1973/0470.html| page=470| language=Norwegian| access-date=2 June 2011}}</ref> He later married [[Siri Sverdrup Lunden]] (1920–2003).

He finished his secondary education in 1938 and graduated from the [[University of Oslo]] with the [[cand.real.]] degree in 1943. He was a [[research assistant]] at the university, and also worked as a chemist and metallurgist for [[Elektrokemisk]] and [[Christiania Spigerverk]]. He was appointed at the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]] in 1945, before being an instructor from 1947 and assistant professor from 1950 at the [[University of Chicago]]. He was appointed as an acting [[docent]] at the Norwegian Institute of Technology in 1952, and after taking his [[dr.techn.]] degree in 1954 he was promoted to professor in 1955.<ref name=hvem/>

He was a member of the [[Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters]], the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]],<ref name=hvem/> and the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27631| title=Gruppe 8: Teknologiske fag| publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]| language=Norwegian| accessdate=2 June 2011| archive-date=19 February 2012| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120219072022/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27631| url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a visiting scholar at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1959 to 1960, the [[University of Wisconsin]] in 1964 and the [[Middle East Technical University]] (for [[UNESCO]]) from 1966 to 1968. He has chaired regional branches of the [[Norwegian Chemical Society]] and the [[Riksmål Society]].<ref name=hvem/> He resided in [[Trondheim]] until his death 1 April 2011.
